title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the 'conjecture fondamentale' from the previous page. That conjecture says dominant morphisms between (limits of) smooth regular schemes of finite type over Q correspond to Γ_Q-compatible exterior homomorphisms of their arithmetic fundamental groups, with E_Q = Γ_Q = Gal(Q̄/Q).

The page sets out the follow-up programme in four steps.

(1) Which outer actions arise. Determine which pro-Galois homotopy types over BQ come from 'modèles élémentaires anabéliens'. Equivalently, for the known geometric groups π_U = π_1(Ū) of such models, determine which outer actions of Γ_Q (and of a second group Γ, which I read as a Teichmüller / Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group, though the reading is uncertain) on these groups are 'possible', i.e. geometric. Elementary models are iterated fibrations in hyperbolic curves (Artin good neighbourhoods), so they are K(π,1).

(2) Other K(π,1) varieties. Ask the same for other profinite groups that are fundamental groups of K(π,1) algebraic varieties over C that are not elementary. Grothendieck names modular varieties, notably moduli of curves M_{g,n}, which are K(π,1) orbifolds through Teichmüller theory.

(3) Gluing. Smooth schemes are covered by elementary neighbourhoods. So from the elementary data one should rebuild, by gluing ('recollement'), a 'truc profini' (a profinite, stack- or topos-like object). It would model the category of smooth schemes over fields of finite type over Q, possibly over arbitrary fields. A second gluing would then recover the category of smooth schemes of finite type over K.

(4) Universal homeomorphisms. This category is to be replaced by its category of fractions obtained by inverting universal homeomorphisms. That is the setting in which the next page states that X ↦ X_et is 1-faithful, and fully faithful after localization.

The page is a programme sketch, not a proof: anabelian reconstruction of the whole category of varieties from Galois-equivariant profinite homotopy types, via K(π,1) elementary neighbourhoods.
errors: The extension 'ou plus gén. sur un corps quelconque' is over-optimistic. Anabelian reconstruction fails over algebraically closed fields, and in general over fields lacking strong arithmetic (e.g. C), and is delicate over finite fields. Known results need fields finitely generated over Q, sub-p-adic fields (Mochizuki), or similar.
The identity of Γ, as distinct from Γ_Q, is unclear on the page. If it is meant as a GT-type group, the analogy is heuristic.

The gluing step is only sketched. Gluing profinite data along elementary neighbourhoods requires controlling the morphisms between overlaps. This is exactly what later rigorous work (étale homotopy types, Schmidt–Stix) had to make precise.

ideas.modern_name: Geometricity / characterisation of outer Galois representations; Grothendieck section and Hom conjectures

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly proposes classifying which outer actions of Γ_Q (and of a Teichmüller-type group Γ) on fundamental groups of non-elementary K(π,1) varieties, especially modular varieties for curves, come from geometry. He treats this as parallel to the elementary case, in order to feed them into the gluing reconstruction. The use of moduli varieties as additional anabelian 'building blocks' for reconstructing categories of varieties is only partially explored today. Most work treats M_{g,n} for GT purposes rather than as gluing pieces.
missed.quote: questions analogues pour d'autres types de groupes profinis, correspondant à des K(π,1) qui se réaliseraient par des variétés algébriques ... mais pas par des variétés élémentaires. (J'ai en vue des variétés modulaires ...)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This suggests extending Schmidt–Stix-style étale-homotopy anabelian reconstruction to orbifold or stacky K(π,1) pieces such as M_{g,n}. That connects GT theory with the anabelian reconstruction programme.

deep.surprise_reason: The programme here (elementary anabelian models, gluing, inverting universal homeomorphisms, modular varieties as K(π,1)) closely matches the letter to Faltings and Esquisse. Its main parts were later realised by Schmidt–Stix and Carlson–Haine–Wolf. The only mildly new nuance is treating modular varieties explicitly as non-elementary K(π,1) blocks in the reconstruction scheme.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely begins '[opér]ations extérieures possibles des groupes ...'; the words after 'des' ('groupes-groupes') and the line 'inerts' are uncertain. The latter may be a marginal insertion such as 'inertie' or a qualifier of the groups.
'dont on munira la cat. des fractions' is uncertain; it may read 'ou mieux, la cat. des fractions' or similar.
